question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I started with the assigned guide, then tried discovery for C# style choices. That search gave no match, and a broader style search was unhelpful, so I read the vocabularies collection to find the registered choice and tier paths. I requested both selected resources together, expecting the choices to provide IDs, property sets, and conflict groups, and the tiers to provide descriptions. The choice response already embedded the tiers, so the separate tier request was unnecessary. After seeing complete scope and property coverage, I had the local data for the five qualifying choices and both groups. I made discovery searches and a full contract request to check whether they stated an explicit rule for omitted Boolean values; they did not add such a rule. I answered using the complete member list and property sets, flagged that interpretation as an inference, and did not pursue individual choice links because they did not identify a missing fact needed for the task.
